title: Global Context Guidance for Diffusion Large Language Models
claim: We build a controlled synthetic benchmark where evidence surrounds masked tokens at varied distances, isolating how models use global versus local context.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, shuffle icon between entity pools and example document
description: The figure shows how a synthetic infilling benchmark is generated. On the left, a gray header reads 'Entity Pools'. Below it are five rounded boxes, each holding sample entities: Clients (Orion, Nova, Vega, Altair), Projects (Beacon, Aurora, Meridian, Zephyr), Code names, Channels, and Owners (Approver-A/B/C). A bold 'Shuffle' label with a crossing-arrows icon sits in the middle and points right. On the right, under a 'Bidirectional Document' header, a rounded box holds templated sentences such as 'Client Orion is assigned to Project Beacon.' Evidence sentences are highlighted peach, distractor sentences gray, and a central sentence has three yellow [MASK] tokens. Vertical ellipses show omitted text. Supporting evidence appears both above and below the masked sentence. A legend at the bottom maps peach to evidence tokens, gray to distractor tokens and yellow to mask tokens. The eye goes first to the yellow masks.
caption: Data generation process for a synthetic infilling benchmark. Entities are randomly sampled from predefined pools and used to construct a bidirectional document. In the resulting document, supporting evidence is placed on both sides of masked tokens, and separated from them by distractor tokens. The distances from the masked tokens to the supporting evidence are varied randomly for each sample.
abstract: Diffusion large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive LLMs, enabling parallel generation through iterative denoising. Recent guidance methods improve diffusion LLMs by introducing a weak model to guide the prediction of the base model during denoising. However, the influence of the weak model during denoising remains less clear, and computing its prediction requires an additional forward pass at each denoising step. We present in this paper an in-depth analysis of how diffusion LLMs use contextual information during denoising. Our analysis reveals that diffusion LLMs rely more heavily on local context while often underutilizing global context. Based on this observation, we introduce Global Context Guidance (GCG), a feature-space guidance method that enhances global-context utilization without constructing an explicit weak model. Extensive experiments on LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B, and LLaDA-1.5 across diverse benchmarks demonstrate that GCG consistently outperforms existing guidance methods, while incurring much lower inference overhead.
